# CANDIDATE: VOLUME_CONFIRMATION_FILTER_RIBBON_RIDE_P

**Filed:** 2026-07-12  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Adding a volume confirmation filter to the ribbon_ride P (BASE) entry condition will improve fill quality by ensuring breakdown bars have sufficient participation, reducing slippage and improving real-fill alignment with simulated entries. This filter targets the existing "no volume divergence" rule by adding a positive volume threshold (breakdown bar volume > 20-bar average volume) to confirm institutional interest, thereby increasing the probability of clean fills without significantly increasing missed opportunity because high-volume breakdowns are more likely to sustain follow-through.

## Mechanism

Entry trigger remains the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup (level rejection + EMA ribbon flip + confluence) but adds a volume confirmation: the breakdown bar's volume must be greater than the 20-period average volume calculated on the 3-minute timeframe prior to the bar. Exit logic remains unchanged (chart stop primary, chandelier profit-lock, premium stop catastrophe cap, TP1 at +50%, runner exit rules). The filter is applied before entry qualification; if volume condition fails, no entry is generated for that trigger.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account scales to ~14% of headline P&L (per OP-20 disclosure 1).  
2. **Sample bias:** Using J's 6 anchor days as sole source of truth risks overfitting to specific microstructure events; filter may perform differently on non-anchor days due to regime-dependent volume characteristics.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward held-out window tested yet).  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no real OPRA fill simulation on top 3 J days performed).  
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: filter may reject all entries on a low-volume breakdown day (e.g., 5/05 loser day) turning a small loss into a zero (helping) or missing a runner (hurting). Max drawdown scenario: filter removes too many winners during low-volume regimes, increasing consecutive losers. Blow-up scenario: false volume spikes during news events trigger entries that immediately reverse, causing cascading stops.  
6. **Concentration:** Unknown; requires full backtest to determine if top-5 days contribute >50% of P&L (if filter removes marginal trades, concentration may increase).

## Pre-merge gate

- Stage-1 backtest on 16-month OPRA data showing:  
  (a) Fill rate improvement (sim-to-real fill ratio) on anchor days ≥ 5% without worsening missed opportunity (measured by reduction in winner P&L < 5% on any anchor day).  
  (b) Gym validators pass (v42+).  
  (c) Real-fills check on top 3 J days shows < ±10% P&L delta vs baseline.  
  (d) Out-of-sample walk-forward (OIS/IS ≥ 0.70) on non-anchor days.

## Confidence

5 / 10 -- Hypothesis is sound but lacks empirical validation; volume filters have historically shown mixed results in 0DTE due to extreme intraday volume spikes. Needs Stage-1 data to confirm fill-rate improvement without anchor regression.
